ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, managers, and authorized signatories against the CSSF sanctions database, the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) alerts, the consolidated EU sanctions list, the UN Security Council sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, and INTERPOL red notices. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any person qualifying as a politically exposed person (PEP), their family members, or known close associates. Risk-based refresh screening is required at minimum every six months and upon any material change in ownership or management. All screening results and supporting evidence must be retained in the AML/KYC file for at least five years after the end of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / eJustice portal - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés de Luxembourg (RCSL)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be composed of Latin-script characters. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet for the RCSL electronic dossier. The name must be distinguishable from all existing registered names, must not be misleading, must not be contrary to public order or good morals, and must be capable of being rendered in French, German, or English in the articles of association. No mandatory use of a specific national language is imposed for the corporate name itself.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCSL refuses a requested name on grounds of indistinguishability, misleading character, or public-order contravention, the applicant must file a written review request with the RCSL Directorate through the LBR e-filing messaging system within fifteen (15) days of the refusal, specifying the grounds of objection and attaching revised name identification evidence. If the RCSL confirms the refusal, an administrative appeal may be lodged before the contentious chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within forty (40) days of notification. For names incorporating sensitive financial or regulated tokens, prior approval from the Ministry of Finance and, where applicable, the CSSF must be obtained before resubmitting. The name reservation may be renewed for successive 30-day periods upon payment of the registry fee, provided no intervening third-party application for the same name has been accepted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is tolerated for the initial RCSL registration only if a separate physical operational site is maintained in Luxembourg and the registered office is not merely a mail-forwarding address. For an international wholesale distribution SARL in the low-risk food-ingredient sector, the Luxembourg tax and corporate authorities apply a substantive-presence test under domestic law and the EU anti-abuse rules. A pure virtual office without real management, bookkeeping, and storage or logistics substance will likely be challenged for Luxembourg tax residence and may lead to administrative strike-off. A corporate services provider's physical office may serve as the registered office on a customer-agreement basis, but ultimate liability for substance remains with the SARL itself.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate; approximately 15% probability of an unannounced physical inspection in the first operating year for a low-risk wholesale exporter. The RCSL and Luxembourg tax inspectorate may conduct on-site checks where substance indicators are weak. The CSSF inspection risk is negligible unless regulated activities are later added.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, Title V (Articles 710-1 to 710-23) governing Sociétés à responsabilité limitée; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register and on annual accounts; Grand-Ducal Regulations on RCS e-filing and publication in the RESA.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) together with the coordinated articles of association (statuts coordonnés), filed electronically with the RCS and published in the Electronic Collection of Companies and Associations (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations, RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SARL must have a minimum subscribed share capital of EUR 12,000. At incorporation the entire capital must be fully subscribed and fully paid up; cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked account with a Luxembourg credit institution or placed in notarial escrow, and may be released to the company only after RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that: (1) the subscribers' applications for ordinary shares are accepted; share capital of EUR 12,000 is fully subscribed and paid up, and release conditions are approved; (2) the coordinated articles of association are adopted; (3) the registered office is set at the address stated in the preamble; (4) [Gérant Name] is appointed first gérant with full day-to-day management authority, acting severally; (5) the gérant is authorized to open bank accounts, appoint signatories, execute the incorporation filing and all ancillary applications with the RCS, Ministry of the Economy, ALVA, tax and social authorities; (6) all actions taken before this resolution are ratified; (7) this resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name verification and capital blocking
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS name search and reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform an online search on the LBR/RCS database to verify that the proposed SARL name is available and not confusingly similar to an existing Luxembourg or European registered company. If available, reserve or confirm the name. Concurrently open a blocked capital account at a Luxembourg credit institution for the EUR 12,000 minimum capital, or instruct the notary to hold the funds in escrow pending incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name with distinctive element
Identity and nationality details of each incorporator
Address proof of incorporators and intended registered office
Bank account opening forms or notary escrow instructions
Draft articles of association for preliminary validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS flags a similarity, submit an alternative name or provide a reasoned distinction memorandum to the Registry; update the draft articles of association accordingly and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public (Notaire) – Chamber of Notaries of Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary reviews all incorporation documents, verifies the legal capacity of the subscribers, confirms the full payment of the subscribed capital, certifies the deed of incorporation and the coordinated articles of association, and ensures that the mandatory legal and regulatory statements are included. The notary will then transmit the deed for RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Draft coordinated articles of association
Original blocked bank account certificate or notary escrow receipt for EUR 12,000
Identification documents and tax residence proofs of each shareholder
Certificate of non-disqualification or court record for the first gérant
Proposed corporate name reservation reference
Draft first board resolution or shareholders' written resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, the application is returned for corrected or supplementary documents; any substantive amendment to the articles requires a fresh signature by all subscribers before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS electronic filing and legal publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) / Luxembourg Business Registers e-filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial deed, coordinated articles, statement of paid-up capital, and annexes through the LBR online filing system or via the notary's electronic channel. The RCS will allocate the corporate registration number and publish a legal notice in the RESA. Obtain the official RCS excerpt as the definitive proof of legal existence.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation
Coordinated articles of association
Proof of capital payment (bank certificate or notary attestation)
Notary's certificate of statutory compliance
Completed RCS registration form (Formulaire A)
Power of attorney if filing through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a formal query, provide written explanations and corrected documents through the portal within the indicated cure period. If the filing is refused, appeal to the local commercial court (Tribunal de l'arrondissement) in accordance with Luxembourg procedural law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business establishment authorization for merchant activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Central Office for Establishment Authorizations (Service des autorisations d'établissement) / Guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the mandatory autorisation d'établissement for the commercial profession of wholesaler/distributor. The application may be submitted online via MyGuichet.lu immediately after RCS registration. Provide the required professional qualification or, if inapplicable, evidence of compliant legal form and financial substance. The authorization covers the wholesale distribution of pre-packaged food products.
required_dossiers: RCS excerpt proving incorporation
Form B1 / business establishment application through MyGuichet.lu
Criminal record extract (bulletin n°3) for the gérant
Professional qualification or diploma certificate evidencing relevant experience
Employment certificates for the gérant if relying on managerial experience
Financial solvency statement, audited or certified by an accountant
Lease contract or title for the registered office and storage premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry questions professional qualifications, submit complementary evidence during the cure period. Refusals may be appealed to the Ministry of the Economy within 40 days from notification; further recourse lies to the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and Administration des contributions directes (ACD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SARL for VAT using the harmonized national form or MyGuichet.lu, providing the RCS number, registered office address, and intended wholesale activity code. The ACD will open the corporate income tax file and assign a Luxembourg tax identification number. Submit an EORI application if cross-border import or export formalities are intended.
required_dossiers: RCS excerpt
Notarized articles of association
Business establishment authorization (or copy of filing acknowledgement)
Registered office address proof
Gérant identification and appointment documents
EORI questionnaire if customs registration is sought
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax administration issues a late-registration notice, submit proof of RCS filing date and explain the administrative sequence. Correct any filing omissions and pay any nominal late fee before the prescribed deadline; if an assessment is raised, file an immediate objection with AEDT.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) – Affiliation department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company and the gérant with the CCSS within eight days of formation. Declare the gérant in the mandatory social security scheme and register any initial employees. Obtain the employer registration number and individual social security numbers for all statutory contributors.
required_dossiers: RCS excerpt
RBS / CCSS employer registration form
Copy of notarized articles
Gérant civil status and address details
Employment contracts or work declaration forms
Identification of beneficial owners if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CCSS alleges late affiliation, file a reasoned explanation with evidence of the RCS registration delay. Requests for retroactive cure are generally accepted when the eight-day statutory period runs from the effective registration date rather than the deed date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food business operator registration and warehouse approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Veterinary and Food Administration (Administration luxembourgeoise vétérinaire et alimentaire, ALVA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company and its storage premises with ALVA as a food business operator handling pre-packaged, shelf-stable foodstuffs. Because the product contains tallow of animal origin, verify whether a specific approval under Regulation (EC) No 853/2004 is required for cold or frozen storage beyond retail. Submit HACCP documentation, storage protocols, and product specification sheets.
required_dossiers: RCS excerpt
Food business operator registration form to ALVA
Site plan and address of the distribution warehouse
HACCP manual or equivalent self-check protocol
Product specification sheet for spicy tallow hotpot soup base
Storage temperature and cold-chain management procedures
Cleaning and pest control contract certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ALVA raises objections regarding hygiene controls, issue a corrective action plan, resubmit the HACCP documentation, and request an on-site verification visit. In case of refusal, file a written reconsideration request with the Director of ALVA within 15 days of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Central Office for Establishment Authorizations and Luxembourg Veterinary and Food Administration (ALVA) for food-chain licensing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Merchant establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) and food business operator registration/approval under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and, if applicable, Regulation (EC) No 853/2004 for storage of tallow-containing food products

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C / Simple registration under the amended Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; a full EIA report is not required for a low-impact wholesale distribution warehouse storing pre-packaged goods. An environmental notification or class 2 authorization may apply if the warehouse cold-storage capacity exceeds the thresholds in the Grand-Ducal Regulation on environmentally classed establishments.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with municipal wastewater discharge limits for commercial premises under Luxembourg water-management law; no significant VOC or combustion emissions expected. Waste handling must respect the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste management, with segregated collection of edible oil/tallow residues, cardboard, packaging plastics, and general waste; discharge of process wastewater containing fats to the public sewer is prohibited without meeting grease-trap standards and municipal authorization.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Administration des services de secours (CAS) for the warehouse and office premises, including smoke detection, fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and structural load assessment for racking. Occupational health and safety clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) covering workplace hazard analysis, electrical installation safety, manual handling training, first-aid equipment, and, where applicable, a traffic management plan for forklifts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB). Prudential supervision of banks and financial intermediaries is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). Luxembourg has no separate central bank foreign exchange control administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg operates a fully liberalised capital and current account regime by virtue of EU obligations under Articles 63/64 TFEU and the Schengen/Euro area arrangements. The euro is fully convertible, with no restrictions on current account transactions, portfolio investment, direct investment, or the repatriation of profits, dividends, liquidation proceeds, or loan repayments for non-resident shareholders. Profit remittance is subject only to compliance with corporate formalities (approval of annual accounts) and applicable withholding tax obligations under Luxembourg domestic tax law and double tax treaties. No prior authorisation from the BCL or the Ministry of Finance is required for cross-border payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender, mandatory sale, or time-limit repatriation rules for export proceeds in Luxembourg. Exporters may retain, reinvest, or transfer export receipts in any currency without conversion obligations. Banks are, however, obliged to report suspected anti-money laundering and terrorist financing incidents under the Luxembourg Criminal Code and the Law of 12 November 2004, and to collect statistical Balance of Payments (BoP) data for the BCL under ECB reporting requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for Luxembourg-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) using the EU Single European Payment Area (SEPA) and PSD2 passport. A fully Luxembourg-licensed EMI with an EBA-compliant e-money authorisation can open virtual accounts and conduct EUR and cross-border settlement, but the SARL's commercial banking function for trade finance, escrow, and documentary credit will require a regulated credit institution. Third-country/offshore EMIs (non-EEA, e.g. some Asia-Pacific or Caribbean e-money operators) are not recognised as qualified payment institutions for Luxembourg corporate treasury purposes and are legally constrained by the Luxembourg Banking Act 1993 and PSD2 restrictions; they cannot lawfully act as the primary clearing rail for the SARL's export distribution without a local branch or agent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is partially mandated. In practice, Luxembourg credit institutions require initial on-site identity verification of at least one senior manager or a resolution-holding director for an SARL capital account and the main operating account. Remote onboarding using eIDAS-qualified electronic signatures, video KYC, and CSSF-accepted digital identity proof is permissible for many banks provided passport scans and certified corporate registry extracts are submitted. However, because the beneficial owner may be a non-EU/offshore entity in the indirect ownership chain, most first-tier banks will demand a physical or discreet audited meeting with the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) in Luxembourg or at a recognized Luxembourg diplomatic/notary post before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from a low-tax/offshore jurisdiction without clear economic nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified source-of-funds letter from the originating bank, audited financial statements of the injecting shareholder, signed intercompany loan/subscription agreement, group organisational chart, business plan for the Luxembourg SARL, and tax domicile certificates for all UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity inconsistent with an ISIC 4638 wholesale seasoning/export distribution business
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full trade cycle documentation, including commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, customs declarations, warehouse receipts, inventory forecasts, dispatch schedules, and sales contracts with end buyers, supplemented by an independent audit confirmation of the expected annual merchandise flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or sanctioned-adjacent beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP declaration, updated CV and business references from an EU-regulated financial intermediary, independent source-of-wealth report prepared by a Luxembourg counsel or certified auditor, UBO register (RBE) extraction, and avoidant sanctions screening reports against EU/UN/US/OFAC consolidated lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Proposed settlement via unlicensed or non-bankable payment service provider in the inbound trade chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg legal opinion confirming the PSP's licensing/exemption status, evidence of authorization in the PSP's home jurisdiction, PSP due-diligence file, transaction flow diagram, and contractual undertakings restricting payments to segregated client accounts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions to the SARL's escrow account must be remitted by SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Credit Transfer using the company's IBAN at a Luxembourg credit institution. The wire must reference the BCL/ECB BoP statistical purpose code corresponding to direct investment equity capital (e.g., the applicable EU/ECB code for 'Direct investment — equity capital' as instructed by the onboarding bank) and include a written remittance narrative: 'Contribution to share capital of LU_SARL, ISIC 4638 wholesale seasoning goods distribution.' The receiving bank will verify the UBO, the triggering ESG/AML screen, and the corporate authorization (boarding resolution). For CNY or USD injections, the aggregation custodian bank should pre-clear the conversion rate and the temporary custody arrangement before credit is allocated to the operational account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for export trade settlements are SWIFT MT103 single-customer payments for full pre-payment, SWIFT MT202 for bank-to-bank cover, documentary collections under URC 522 for low-risk open account flows, and irrevocable commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 for buyer-payee risk. For EU/SEPA counterparties, a SEPA Credit Transfer with the related reference 'Hotpot Base Brick Wholesale Distribution' is sufficient. For Chinese or Hong Kong settlement nodes, RMB/CNH clearing through Bank of China Luxembourg or CIPS-participant correspondent accounts may be used, supported by underlying trade documents and VAT/customs evidence to avoid FX revert or trade-based money-laundering red flags.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward contracts (EUR/CNY, EUR/USD, CNY/USD) entered into with an authorised Luxembourg or EU credit institution under ISDA terms with documented underlying trade exposure.
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/CNY or EUR/USD) for hedging long-term working capital requirements and trusted debt-service cash flows, subject to EMIR clearing and variation margin obligations.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on offshore CNY (CNH) where a leg or notional conversion is subject to partial convertibility barriers of the underlying Asian currency, only with a licensed global FX clearing bank and ISO 20022 payment reconciliation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of RCS Registration Data (Confirmation annuelle RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 January and 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic removal from register (radiation d'office) and administrative dissolution after repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS through the e-RCS electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of financial year-end, e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines up to EUR 1,000; court-ordered filing; administrative strike-off if persistently delinquent

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Register Confirmation (Confirmations des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 and/or imprisonment for intentional failure to file

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Luxembourg Corporate Income Tax Return (Déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu collectivités, Form eux)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (Luxembourg direct tax authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the following tax year for 31 December year-end; extension to 31 March of the second following year available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing interest of 0.8% per month on unpaid tax; penalty up to 10% of tax due; ex officio assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net Wealth Tax Return (Déclaration d'impôt sur la fortune, IF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as corporate income tax return, generally 31 May following the assessment year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Increased 10% late filing penalty; statutory arrears interest; ex officio assessment

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for SARL when two of three criteria are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total > EUR 4.4M; net turnover > EUR 8.8M; average employees > 50. Public-interest entities require audit regardless of thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies and related regulations); IFRS permitted for non-listed entities, mandatory for public-interest entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: File annual confirmation of all registered beneficial owners via RBE portal by 31 March; any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership must be filed within one month of that change; unfiled confirmations trigger rejection and administrative fines

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $8,500 – $21,600 for a Luxembourg SME audit (approx EUR 8,000–20,000)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate effective CIT rate in Luxembourg City (17% corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge = 18.19%, plus municipal business tax of 6.75%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 80% IP box exemption on net qualifying IP income; 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and 80% exemption on qualifying capital gains under Sec. 166 LIR; new business investment tax credit; full deduction of interest (subject to ATAD interest limitation at 30% EBITDA); minimum net wealth tax of EUR 3,540 per year with asset-based component; Pillar Two top-up applies only to groups with revenue ≥ EUR 750 million

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 620 (Déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu business portal / eCDF interbank channel; separate Form 610 for net wealth tax
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end (e.g., FY 2025 return due 31 December 2026); a 6-month extension is automatically available via the portal upon request, further extension only with justified cause

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form (SARL), registered corporate name, registered office, RCS Luxembourg number, establishment licence (autorisation d'établissement), and fiscal matricule of the Luxembourg entity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Completed by the local tax agent/accountant; non-resident shareholders are not required to be listed individually on the corporate return

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the accounting period; a first period may extend up to 12 months
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Match the statutory financial statements; for a newly incorporated SARL, the first return covers the period from incorporation to the first year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net business result before tax from the P&L: gross margin from wholesale distribution of pre-packaged spicy tallow hotpot soup base bricks less cost of goods sold, distribution costs, and operating expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Luxembourg-based distributor owned by a non-resident parent, the commercial result must reflect the arm's length compensation agreed in the intercompany distribution agreement

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest, dividends, royalties, and other investment income received from third parties or related entities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify each dividend source so the 12-month holding requirement for the participation exemption can be verified; interest on shareholder loans must be benchmarked at arm's length

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of expenses non-deductible for CIT: municipal business tax, net wealth tax, 50% of director fees, excessive representation costs, fines, gifts, and amounts failing the documentation test
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Group management fees recharged by a foreign parent must be supported by a written cost allocation agreement and an adequate benchmark; otherwise the add-back is imposed automatically

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of 100% of qualifying dividend income and 80% of qualifying capital gains derived from shareholdings meeting the participation-exemption conditions under Article 166 LIR
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owner must provide the subsidiary's tax residence certificate and proof of the ≥10% shareholding and the 12-month minimum holding period where applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of 80% of net qualifying IP income (qualifying patents, copyrighted software, and similar assets) to the extent the asset is developed or improved by the Luxembourg entity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Applicable only where the SARL owns or co-owns qualifying intangibles; a pure distributor not holding IP has no eligible IP income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year tax losses carried forward under Article 110 LIR within the 17-year limitation window; losses from tax years before 2026 remain eligible without time limit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure no change-of-control occurred that would restrict loss utilisation; a letterbox acquisition triggers reassessment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final net taxable income subject to the 17% CIT rate; based on the commercial result after all statutory deductions and add-backs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The fiduciary must sign the electronic declaration; the tax office verifies the base against the audited financial statements filed with the RCS

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of Luxembourg-source dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-resident recipients and the applicable withholding tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL acts as withholding agent for the 15% domestic dividend WHT; treaty-reduced rates require a valid TRC and the Luxembourg WHT form (annex) submitted before payment

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Automatic late-payment interest of 0.8% per month on any unpaid CIT, municipal business tax, and WHT; procedural fine of up to EUR 2,500 for late filing or failure to provide information; ex-officio assessment (taxation d'office) of the taxable base with disallowance of unproven deductions; additional surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax for non-cooperation; in cases of deliberate misdeclaration, criminal fraud penalties apply (see fatal red flags)

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic withholding tax on resident and non-resident dividend recipients; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (≥10% interest held ≥12 months or a 24-month indicative holding); most income tax treaties reduce the rate to 5% for portfolio investors and 0% for qualifying corporate shareholdings
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Step 1: Obtain a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the recipient's home tax authority covering the payment year. Step 2: Submit the TRC and the Luxembourg reduced-withholding application form (Form 572 for DTA relief, or the Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption annex) to the Luxembourg Administration des contributions directes or the paying agent before the payment date. Step 3: The paying SARL applies the treaty rate at source or, if WHT was already deducted, the excess is reclaimed by filing a refund request within the statutory limitation period (generally no later than 31 December of the third year following the WHT year). Step 4: Maintain a current substance file and documentary trail in Luxembourg to sustain the benefit on audit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law imposes 0% WHT on interest and royalties paid to non-residents, with two exceptions: payments on profit-participating loans and payments to recipients in EU-listed non-cooperative jurisdictions (15% WHT from 1 January 2022). Most Luxembourg tax treaties provide 0% WHT on interest and royalties, and the EU Interest-Royalties Directive eliminates withholding between associated enterprises in different EU member states.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File mandatory where the group's consolidated annual turnover equals or exceeds EUR 50 million (Law of 23 June 2016); Country-by-Country Report mandatory where the group's consolidated turnover equals or exceeds EUR 750 million; documentation must include functional analysis, benchmark study, and intercompany contracts in EUR
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no standalone ESR statute comparable to the UAE, but substance is decisive through several binding channels: the judicial anti-abuse doctrine (abus de droit), ATAD rules (30% EBITDA interest limitation, CFC rules, general anti-abuse provision), participation-exemption conditions, and the requirement of real activity for a Luxembourg Tax Residence Certificate. For a SARL operating as a wholesale exporter of pre-packaged hotpot soup base, tested substance includes a Luxembourg office, qualified sales and logistics staff, genuine negotiation and invoicing activity, local ERP and bank accounts, warehousing or third-party logistics contracts, risk assumption, and board meetings in Luxembourg. A pure letterbox distributor could lose treaty benefits and the participation exemption, and face re-assessment of profits as if earned by a fully substantive local distributor.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a knowingly false Form 620: understating export revenues from pre-packaged hotpot soup base sales, creating fictitious supplier invoices, inflating deductible expenses, or concealing Swiss or Asian bank accounts used for Swift TT settlement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years and a fine of EUR 250 to EUR 125,000 per infraction under Article 1193 of the Luxembourg General Tax Code; in aggravated or organised fraud, fines up to EUR 250,000, confiscation of proceeds, and publication of the judgment; the underpaid tax is recaptured with monthly interest of 0.8% and penalty interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Any director or gérant who signs or causes the false return is criminally liable as co-principal, with personal imprisonment, fines, and a management ban (interdiction de gérer); the investigating judge may seize the director's passport (travel ban); civil liability attaches for the underpaid tax plus damages under Article 510-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement (Abus de Droit and Treaty Abuse)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SARL as a letterbox with no staff, no office, no local decision-making, and routing intercompany profit flows on undocumented commission or mark-up arrangements to avoid CIT and dividend withholding tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Luxembourg tax administration recaptures the avoided tax at the statutory 24.94% aggregate rate, applies 0.8% monthly late-payment interest, denies treaty benefits and the participation exemption, and may issue a penalty assessment under the GAAR; cross-border information exchange (DAC6, CbCR) increases detection probability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors remain personally liable for intentionally facilitating sham structures: joint and several liability for the recaptured corporate tax and WHT, disqualification from corporate office, personal fines, and imprisonment where the arrangement is qualified as tax fraud; asset tracing and freezing orders may target the director's personal bank accounts

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Administrative Non-Compliance: Late Filing and Non-Payment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing the 31 December Form 620 filing deadline, failing to pay the CIT instalments (usually due 30 June and 31 December of the assessment year), or failing to remit the 15% dividend WHT within the statutory payment period
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Ex-officio assessment with complete disallowance of undocumented deductions; penalty interest of 0.8% per month compounded; procedural fines up to EUR 2,500; forced recovery through garnishment of the SARL's bank accounts and seizure of goods; non-declaration of WHT triggers a specific charge of 10% of the withheld amount plus the monthly interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the company's tax debts arise from intentional or negligent conduct, directors may be declared jointly liable for the full unpaid tax debt upon liquidation or insolvency; the director's personal assets can be attached; travel bans are possible in enforcement proceedings when the director leaves Luxembourg to frustrate collection

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML Non-Compliance in Trade Payment Processes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to conduct KYC/AML due diligence on Asian and European counterparties involved in Swift TT and Letter-of-Credit settlements for hotpot soup base exports; processing payments without identifying beneficial owners, or failing to report suspicious transactions to the Luxembourg FIU (Cellule de Renseignement Financier - CRF)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg AML framework, legal persons face administrative fines up to EUR 5 million and criminal sanctions including confiscation of transaction funds; the business licence (autorisation d'établissement) can be revoked, freezing the company's operations; repeated violations trigger automatic blacklisting by the banking sector
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute or permit non-compliant cross-border payments are criminally liable with imprisonment up to 5 years and personal fines; civil liability covers the company's AML penalties; the CSSF and CRF can order the director's removal from management and impose a professional ban; passport seizure may accompany criminal investigations
